solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dangerous situation where straight tackles ending in minor gains

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, so the first word grips the next pieces

parts.note: straight means truthful, honest

indicators.note: the final letter of the word minor is the one taken

parts.note: nets is a verb meaning gains or earns

explanation.surface: A small win leads into a perilous position, as if an honest player took on a risky challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackles' reads as a sporting challenge but means grips or holds; 'where' is only a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirred-up insect colony is the standard idiom for a situation full of trouble and hostility.

clue.text: Vacuous homage a nonsense, irritating thing

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so the word homage loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: nonsense is rubbish, trash

explanation.surface: A dismissive critic calls an empty tribute rubbish and an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly skin rash brought on by hot weather is literally an irritating thing.

clue.text: Dance party taking place south of European capital

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below, so the later pieces follow the capital

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
a do is a party
on means happening, as in 'the show is on'

explanation.surface: A party is being held somewhere below a European capital city, with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Baroque court dance in duple time, of Provençal origin.

clue.text: Follow leaders in Election Night Special uttering expletives

indicators.note: the leaders of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Swearing breaks out on a special election-night broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result, the way events succeed one another.

clue.text: Teacher drinking endless coffee, one on a motorbike?

indicators.note: one who drinks takes something inside, so the teacher's title holds the next piece

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for coffee is cut off

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: A teacher sipping coffee rides along on a motorbike.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example; the answer is also a cocktail, which suits 'drinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled passenger car attached to the side of a motorcycle carries a rider.

clue.text: Greek character partial to ethanol is perking up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
partial means only part of the following words is used, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone fond of alcohol finds it livens them up, said of a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' takes NOLISPE from 'ethanol is perking'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the sense of a letter.

clue.text: Pass beyond outskirts of Rimini during trip, one flying over Italian embassy, perhaps?

definitions.text: one flying over Italian embassy, perhaps?

indicators.note: during means inside the span of, so the trip word surrounds what comes before

parts.note: a tour is a trip

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the pass follows the outskirts
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses a mountain pass past the edge of Rimini on an Italian trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb but is the noun for a mountain gap; the definition is by example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's green, white and red flag is a three-coloured banner, hoisted over its embassies.

clue.text: Crack running this way and that

indicators.note: the letters read the same in either direction, forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A crack spreads in all directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack in the sense of a wisecrack is a joke.

clue.text: Unpleasant matter about right for filthy fashion?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sticky stuff goes round the next piece

parts.note: gunge is British slang for sticky, unpleasant matter

explanation.surface: Something nasty that's apt for a grubby style of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1990s style of deliberately scruffy dress, whose name also means dirt, hence filthy fashion.

clue.text: Sound politician, British author

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard, a homophone of what follows

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: A level-headed politician who is also a British writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' seems to praise the politician but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was the English novelist who wrote Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.

clue.text: Giant proves quarrelsome, sapped of energy

indicators.note: sapped of means drained of, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: one who argues is being quarrelsome
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A huge figure turns combative, then runs out of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the hundred-eyed giant set by Hera to guard Io.

clue.text: Poor old king, it's recalled, put in river

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the river surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters of it's are read backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters
Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the old Egyptian king

explanation.surface: A tale of a poor former king, reminisced about and dumped in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns ITS into STI; with TUT it goes 'in' DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless, utterly lacking money: a straight synonym for poor.

clue.text: Censor in decline given extremes of popular novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A censor's power fades while a popular novel flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges DECLINE plus P and R (the ends of 'popular').
explanation.definitionFit: To cut text, as an editor marking deletions in coloured ink; the verb means to censor.

clue.text: Welsh name not starting — something stopped?

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Morgan is a common Welsh name

explanation.surface: A Welshman's name is cut short, leaving something halted.
explanation.walkthrough: The church instrument has stops, knobs that select its pipes, so it is something 'stopped'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe instrument is played with stops, so it is jokingly described as stopped.

clue.text: Dribble ending on knickers, one throwing up?

indicators.note: the ending of the word knickers is its final letter

parts.note: a lobber tosses a ball high into the air

explanation.surface: Someone vomits, with an unfortunate dribble landing on underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' suggests being sick; it is someone hitting a ball upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saliva running from the mouth is drool or dribble.

clue.text: Queen admitted to old club where cheap food served

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the queen goes within the club

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, the two-wood
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen gets into an old club that serves cheap food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a social club; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal French-style restaurant serving inexpensive meals.

clue.text: Twelve numbers, back to back

indicators.note: two copies placed back to back, one facing each way, make a symmetrical run

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number; written forwards and then backwards it gives this leaf

explanation.surface: Twelve numbers lined up back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: NO (number) is set back to back with itself, so the second copy reads ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock.

clue.text: A great fiddler, one not believing in integrity, initially

parts.note: a pagan does not hold the established faith

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of integrity is used

explanation.surface: A great swindler is an unbeliever when it comes to honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddler' suggests a cheat, fitting the integrity theme; it is a violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian virtuoso violinist, and fiddler is slang for violinist.

clue.text: Probable failure grounded after failing

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Something likely to fail, grounded after it failed.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor expected to lose is the one tipped to fail.

clue.text: Nation close to freedom fighter

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous boxer

explanation.surface: A country is on the brink of freedom thanks to a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked West African country.

clue.text: Scent anger

definitions.meaning: perfume burned to give a fragrant smoke
verb: to enrage, to make furious

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, the noun is aromatic smoke and the verb (stressed on the second syllable) means to enrage.

clue.text: One's drawn a hound, one in brown

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: in means inside, so the numeral goes within the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is sketching a dog, one with a brown coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests sketching; it means pulled across a window or stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is something drawn open or shut, over a window or a stage.

clue.text: Agree on origins of remarkably arcane monster

parts.note: to chime is to agree, as in 'chime with'

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Two parties agree about the beginnings of a strangely mysterious monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing creature of Greek myth combining lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Speaker in court before judge, upstanding

indicators.note: before means coming first, so the courting word leads

parts.note: to woo is to court romantically

indicators.note: upstanding means standing up; in a down entry the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ref is short for referee, one who judges a match

explanation.surface: A speaker in a law court addresses an upright judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court; it is the verb to woo. 'upstanding' turns REF into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudspeaker unit designed to reproduce low bass frequencies.

clue.text: See cuckoo welcoming better flight

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the shuffled letters surround the next piece
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Look at a cuckoo greeting a superior bird in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' and 'flight' paint a bird scene, but the bird is the anagram signal and flight means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the sense of fleeing, a getaway.

clue.text: Middle of crowd, a relative place of safety

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: In the middle of a crowd, a relative is a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert, by extension any refuge.

clue.text: Pottery feature in the picture

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
to be in the picture is to be informed

explanation.surface: A piece of pottery features in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the picture' reads as part of the scene; it means informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain or ceramic dishes, the fine pottery first made in the East.

clue.text: Opponent caught in trick

parts.note: someone anti something is opposed to it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An opposing player gets caught playing a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper or absurd prank, a playful trick.

clue.text: Cologne newspaper embraced by the nation

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the nation wraps round the paper

parts.note: France is the nation in mind
rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A paper from Cologne is welcomed across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' reads as the German city; it is eau de cologne.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a scented toilet water, hence a perfume or pleasant smell.

clue.text: Bolt pulled back to secure first of inmates in group of three

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the reversed letters enclose the next piece
pulled back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to bolt is to dart, dash

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A prison bolt is drawn back to lock in an inmate among three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled back' turns DART into TRAD; 'to secure' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three things or people, a trio.

clue.text: Speaker's mocking whiskey ingredient

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what is heard, the sound of the following word

parts.note: wry means drily mocking

explanation.surface: A speaker makes a mocking remark about a whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal grain distilled into American and Canadian whiskey.

clue.text: Is a Bayeux tapestry arrow so beautiful?

definitions.text: Is a Bayeux tapestry arrow so beautiful?

parts.words: Is a Bayeux tapestry arrow so beautiful?
parts.note: the tapestry shows King Harold struck in the eye by an arrow, so it literally grabbed his eye; the phrase also means striking

explanation.definitionFit: Strikingly attractive, drawing attention; the arrow that killed Harold in 1066 grabbed the king's eye.
